sections.title: Taxonomy and general form
sections.text: Schizosaccharomyces pombe is a unicellular yeast in the phylum Ascomycota. In vegetative growth its cells are cylindrical rods with rounded ends; typical dimensions are about 7–14 µm long and 4 µm in diameter, varying with cell cycle and culture conditions. It does not form a mushroom-like fruiting body with a cap and stem.

sections.title: Cell wall and organization
sections.text: The cell is enclosed by a glucan-rich cell wall and a plasma membrane; its cytoplasm contains a nucleus and other eukaryotic organelles. The cutaway in the plate is schematic and does not show their exact positions or proportions to scale. The outer surface is a cell wall, not a fruiting surface bearing gills or pores.

sections.title: Growth and fission
sections.text: The cell elongates mainly by growth at its ends. During division, a contractile ring forms at the middle and a new cell-wall septum grows inward, perpendicular to the long axis. The septum has a primary layer between two secondary layers; its cleavage releases two daughter cells of comparable length. This is medial fission, not budding.

sections.title: Research use and limits
sections.text: This yeast is a widely used model organism for studying cell shape, the cell cycle, and cytokinesis. General microscopic appearance alone is not sufficient to identify an unknown yeast. Food status is not assessed here; this entry is not consumption or food-safety advice.

traits: Microscopic unicellular ascomycete yeast; cells are cylindrical rods with rounded ends
Vegetative cells typically 7–14 µm long and about 4 µm wide; dimensions vary with cell cycle and culture
Growth mainly at cell ends; vegetative division by medial fission, without budding
Medial septum with one primary layer flanked by two secondary layers, shown schematically
Cell-biology model organism; no cap-and-stem fruit body, gills, or pores
safetyNote: Taxonomic and biological reference. This entry is not for identifying an unknown yeast and gives no consumption or food-safety advice.
